events.objective: Establish the symptom timeline and blast radius. Determine when api-gateway p99 latency first exceeded baseline (onset time, to the minute) and whether 504s/errors are confined to /v1/portfolio/* or affect other routes. For the portfolio request path, identify which downstream services show elevated latency/error/resource anomalies (CPU, memory, connection pool, GC) starting at or before onset. Report per-service first-anomaly timestamps so we can tell whether the gateway is the origin or a downstream call is.

Enumerate everything that changed in the window 2026-03-09T22:00Z to now across ALL services, not just api-gateway: deployments, config changes, feature flags. Include the reported gateway HTTP/2 upgrade, and specifically flag any changes to services on the /v1/portfolio/* call path or to shared components (load balancer, service mesh, DNS, DB, cache). For each change give exact time and service owner. Also retrieve the portfolio path dependency graph (what api-gateway calls, and what those call) to identify shared components.

Using the onset time from task a and the change list from task b, correlate timing: which changes preceded onset, and do prior historical incidents match this signature (gateway latency + portfolio route timeouts)? Search historical incidents for cases where gateway latency was a downstream symptom, or where an HTTP/2/upstream upgrade caused timeouts, and report precedent, prior root cause, and fix.

The /v1/portfolio/* chain is api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> {ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache)}; market-data-service -> redis-cache and exchange-gateway. ledger-db is shared by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; redis-cache is shared by auth-service, portfolio-service and market-data-service. Both datastores are flagged shared:true, owner platform.

These are leads only.

No deployment in the window was rolled back (get_deployments returned only dep-5220 with rolled_back_at null) and no changes were logged for ledger-db, redis-cache, DNS, load balancer or service mesh in the config-change result.

events.statement: Full change list in the window 2026-03-09T22:00Z–11:59Z contains exactly one deployment and two config changes: dep-5220 api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00Z ('envoy 1.29 -> 1.30', 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service', rolled_back_at null, status live), cfg-2199 order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2 at 07:00Z, cfg-2207 portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 09:52Z ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'). No change to ledger-db, redis-cache, DNS, LB or mesh, and no rollback.

Timing correlation: onset (gateway/portfolio-service first anomaly in the 09:50Z bucket, 09:50–09:52Z) is 110 minutes AFTER the 08:00Z gateway HTTP/2 deploy but coincides (same minute) with cfg-2207 portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 09:52:00Z. The gateway deploy cannot explain a 09:50 onset without a delayed trigger; the pool cut is the only change at onset.

Historical precedent with the closest signature match is HIST-116 (2025-12-18, api-gateway, match_score 6): 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade', symptoms '504 at gateway','upstream resets','timeouts', category bad_deployment, prior root cause 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default', fix 'Rolled back gateway'.

A second precedent that matches the current service path rather than the gateway: HIST-115 (2025-09-25, order-service, match_score 7): symptoms 'connection is not available','request timed out','pool exhausted', category config_change, root cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', fix 'Reverted config; added validation'. This mirrors cfg-2207 (pool size cut via a profile) on the portfolio-service->ledger-db edge.

Precedent HIST-102 (2025-09-02, portfolio-service + ledger-db) shows the exact symptom pair 'portfolio page timeouts','504 at gateway' with prior root cause 'Unplanned ledger-db primary failover; 6 min of refused connections' and fix 'Failover completed; added retry'; HIST-110 (2026-01-15) shows ledger-db-side slowness ('statement timeouts','slow queries', root cause 'Cloud volume burst credits exhausted; IOPS throttled') propagating to order latency. Both are leads showing a datastore fault can surface as gateway 504s on this path.

Dependency graph confirms the /v1/portfolio/* chain and its shared components: portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db, shared:true, owner platform), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache, shared:true, owner platform); market-data-service -> redis-cache and exchange-gateway; api-gateway -> portfolio-service. ledger-db and redis-cache are the two shared nodes through which a neighbour could injure portfolio-service.

events.description: No telemetry was retrieved for ledger-db or redis-cache (connection-pool saturation, IOPS, GC) in this session; the change list shows no change to those components, so the shared-datastore path could not be ruled in or out from change data alone.

Neither the deployment nor config-change results include an explicit effective-propagation time for cfg-2207 (commit vs pod reload of db.pool.max_size); whether the pool cut takes effect immediately or on restart/reload decides whether 09:52 is cause or coincidence.
No post-09:52 gateway/portfolio-service metric was examined to see whether rolling back cfg-2207 or dep-5220 restores latency; no such remediation event appears in the change list.

events.answer: Correlation: the only change at onset is cfg-2207 — portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50→5 at 09:52:00Z, landing in the same minute as the first gateway/portfolio-service latency anomaly (09:50–09:52Z bucket). The suspected gateway v9.3.0 HTTP/2 deploy (dep-5220, envoyer 1.29→1.30) preceded onset by ~110 minutes (08:00Z) and had no rollback, so timing does not favor it as the trigger. Historical precedent: HIST-116 is the closest gateway-latency match (envoy HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams default, fixed by rolling back the gateway), but HIST-115 (datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile → 'connection is not available'/'request timed out'/'pool exhausted', fixed by reverting config) matches the pool-cut mechanism, and HIST-102 confirms the exact 'portfolio page timeouts + 504 at gateway' pair can originate at ledger-db. Precedents are leads, not causes.
